notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) recorded at head d04061d, all rc 0, uncommitted false, each model_id matching its tier (other model names in the transcripts appear only in the environment text). reads is empty in all five; the tool calls are Write, Bash, Edit and, in haiku-1 and haiku-2, a Read of their own webhook.ex, with no Skill call. In the scratch folder (Elixir 1.20.3) all five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; opus-1 (line 96) and sonnet-1 (lines 96, 105) fail mix format --check-formatted, matching format_ok. No run has a doctest (no iex> prompt anywhere).

Rules changed since ba24972 (git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/): the head rule was rewritten and the required-keys rule gained three paragraphs; ex_unit.md's capture_log section gained a sentence that no graded rule here depends on. The other seven graded rules are unchanged and follow the 2026-10-22-d standard.

In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use: graded against the new text, 0 of 5 violated. The deciding sentence is "A head binds what selects its clause: a value matched against a literal, a value a guard reads, or a key whose presence selects, because another clause catches the input that lacks it.", with the parse paragraph ("those keys select the clause by their presence, so they belong in the head even when the guard reads none of them"). Under the ba24972 text haiku-2 (created, lines 39-40), sonnet-1 (id, type, created, lines 75-76) and sonnet-2 (created, lines 76-77) would have been violated; opus-1 and haiku-1 bind only guard-read keys and are clean under both texts.

Head-rule bullets in the case file, runs violating out of 5. Presence bullet (the parse head matches the keys it requires, with a clause below that catches a payload lacking them): 0 violated; haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 follow it; opus-1 matches only "type" in the head and reads id, created and data in the body with Map.get-based fetch/3 that names each missing key, so its check is marked missed but nothing the rule forbids appears (the Map.get is counted under Read required keys). Moved-pattern bullet (no selecting pattern moved into a body read with dot access that raises): 0 of 5; no run reads a payload key with dot access or a body match. Clutter bullet (no body-only field bound in every head of a 3+-clause function or in a spread multi-clause head): 0 of 5; no 3+-clause function destructures a field (build/3 and parse_data/2 take data whole), every wrapped parse/1 head wraps only for its guard, and sonnet-2's fetch_money/1 (lines 162-164) is the one head that spreads over three lines while binding only guard-read keys, the boundary the bullet allows.

Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys, per sentence, runs violating out of 5: first paragraph (Map.get or brackets on a required key) 2 (opus-1 line 102 Map.get with a nil clause in fetch/3; sonnet-2 line 172 data["amount"]); new re-match sentence ("A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long.") 0, not exercised (no body pattern on a held value; the payload keys are strings); nested-chain and get_in/1 sentences not exercised; Map.fetch/2 sentence 0: opus-1's line 100 comment says it treats a JSON null as missing on purpose, so absent and nil do not need different handling there, and its verdict rests on the unchanged first paragraph, as 2026-10-22-b graded the identical opus-1 fetch_string/2.

Chain fallible steps with `with`, violating runs out of 5: one-step with 3 (opus-1 line 67 and haiku-1 line 106 by "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`"; sonnet-2 line 78 by "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step", its body calls build/3); else 0; case nested in a with body 0.

Naming, violating runs out of 5 per sentence: get/fetch 3 (opus-1 fetch/3 and fetch_optional/3, sonnet-1 three fetch_*, sonnet-2 fetch_string/2 and fetch_money/1); every other sentence 0. data holding the payload's "data" map is allowed in every run; base, envelope, fields, object, body, email, reason and code are not counted, as earlier grades did not count object or event_data.

Closest calls. opus-1's line 100 comment ("# A JSON null counts as missing for required fields.") is read as a why comment, so Opus is clean on Comments; counted, Opus would be violated. opus-1's ## Example in parse/1's @doc is a plain code block, not a doctest; graded clean as a @doc without examples was in earlier sweeps. haiku-2's line 150 comment is counted under Comments on the 2026-10-22-d precedent (opus-1's comment naming the Fields helpers). sonnet-1 line 85 and sonnet-2 line 173 are counted under the struct rule's "Do not guess the missing field from which other keys matched" on the 2026-10-22-b precedent, although both answers are right in the probe: each names the invalid field by elimination, not by checking it. haiku-2's missing-as-invalid is counted under Match every expected shape only, as in 2026-10-22-d.

Probe of 26 payloads in the scratch folder: every run returns an unsupported-type error for "invoice.paid" and reports a known type without amount as a field error. opus-1 and sonnet-1 name every missing and invalid top-level and data field; sonnet-2 names missing top-level keys but gives :invalid_payload for an ill-typed id or type or non-map data; haiku-1 gives :malformed_payload and haiku-2 :invalid_payload for any top-level problem. haiku-2 reports every missing data field as {:invalid_field, key}. sonnet-1 accepts "currency" => "EURO"; the others reject it. haiku-1 treats customer_email as required; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 accept a refund without amount.

Compared with the 2026-10-22-d baseline: the head rule moves from violated to clean in all three tiers, the effect of the rewording (see above). Opus moves from clean to violated on Read required keys (Map.get in fetch/3) and from violated to clean on Comments, and stays violated on the with rule and Naming. Haiku moves from violated to clean on Read required keys and stays violated on Match every expected shape, the with rule and Comments, and clean on Naming. Sonnet moves from clean to violated on Read required keys (sonnet-2 brackets) and on the struct rule (two inferred invalid fields), and stays violated on the with rule, Naming and Comments. Atoms and the return-tuple rule stay clean in every tier.
